Primary outcomes are: (a) Failure of the procedure (Method failure) and complications: the proportion of all cases that were accepted into the study who complied with the protocol but experienced incomplete abortion or ongoing pregnancy and underwent MVA to complete their abortion; and post-abortion complication rates (b) ?Potential? failure and ?potential? side-effect rates: the total number of women who were accepted into the study and experienced incomplete abortion or experienced side-effects, respectively, plus the total number of women wrongly classified by the study provider as eligible (ie within 56 days gestation) and subsequently disqualified, as a percentage of all women who continued in the study plus those so disqualified. (TimePoints: Not Applicable)
secondary_outcome: Secondary outcomes are: (a) Failure to assess GA and abortion status (Assessment failure): the proportion of all clients who underwent two pelvic examinations for whom the study provider?s assessment did not match that of the verifier provider and those for whom the final assessment of abortion status did not match on Day 15/21. (b) Failure to comply (Compliance failure): includes two components: (a) the percentage of women who did not comply with the protocol, that is, did not ingest the misoprostol on schedule, or did not return for follow up at the assigned date and time but either returned at an earlier or later date or could be traced at the given address; and (b) loss to follow up, that is, the percentage of women who received mifepristone but did not return on Day 3 and/or Day 15/21 and could not be followed up at the address provided and the percentage of women who took both mifepristone and misoprostol but did not return on Day 15/21 and could not be followed up at the address provided. brief_summary: CONTEXT: The availability of trained abortion providers is limited in India. Allowing ayurvedic physicians and nurses to perform medication abortions may improve womenâ€™s access to the procedure, but it is unclear whether these clinicians can provide these services safely and effectively. METHODS: Allopathic physicians, ayurvedic physicians and nurses (10 of each), none of whom had experience in abortion provision, were trained to perform medication abortions. In 2008â€“2010, these providers performed medication abortions in five clinics in Bihar and Jharkhand for 1,225 women with a pregnancy of up to eight weeksâ€™ gestation. A two-sided equivalence design was used to test whether providersâ€™ assessments of client eligibility and completeness of abortion matched those of an experienced physician â€œverifier,â€ and whether medication abortions performed by nurses and ayurvedic physicians were as safe and effective as those done by allopathic physicians. RESULTS: Failure rates were low (5â€“6%), and those for nurses and ayurvedic physicians were statistically equivalent to those for allopathic physicians. Provider assessments of client eligibility and completeness of abortion differed from those of the verifier in only a small proportion of cases (3â€“4% for eligibility and 4â€“5% for completeness); these proportions, and rates of loss to follow-up, were statistically equivalent among provider types. No serious complications were observed, and services by all three groups of providers were acceptable to women. CONCLUSION: Findings support amending existing laws to improve womenâ€™s access to medication abortion by expanding the provider base to include ayurvedic physicians and nurses.

public_title: Promotion of Cognitive function like memory, attention and learning among the elderly people
scientific_title: A double blind placebo controlled clinical trial of a ayurveda formulation beneficial in the prevention and management of cognitive deficit disorders
study_design: Randomized, Parallel Group, Active Controlled Trial
intervention_name: Test formulation 500mg twice per day for a period of six months
intervention_description: 500mg capsule was prepared with the help of additive and effective dose of each plant extract was determined during pre-clinical studies. The test formulation was given in two divided doses 1 capsule morning and 1 capsule evening (8am after breakfast and 8 pm after meals) The dried whole plant of Bacopa monnieri and Centella asiatica, root of Withania somnifera and fruits of Hippophae rhamnoides were utilized to obtain hydro-methanolic extract. The extract of each plant was utilized for identification of active compound present in each plant. For this purpose chromatographic separation were done by using TLC, HPLC and HPTLC. After determination of active compound the molecular characterization were done with the help of IR and NMR.
comparator: Placebo 500mg twice per day for a period of six months (Placebo capsule were prepared (by using dicalcium phosphate-300mg, starch-100mg, calcium carbonate-100mg) similar to test drug and administered in similar manner to test drug. Both normal elderly cases as well as diagnosed cases of senile dementia of Alzheimer?s type were treated with the test formulation and another group with placebo as per schedule.

brief_summary: When the hydro-alcoholic extract of Bacopa monnieri, Centela asiatica, Withania somnifera and Hippophae rhamnoides in effective doses was administered in combine form orally to normal elderly as well as SDAT patients showed improvement in cognitive function, as mini-mental state examination scores, memory and attention span scores were found to be improved and no further decline was noticed. The test formulation exerted neuro-modulatory activity by regulating 5-HT and nor-adrenaline, reducing inflammatory markers like IL-6, TNF-Î± and acting on oxidative stress markers. An overall improvement in mental health status by improving memory and cognition, sleep, psychotic behavior and general feeling of well being was observed among senile dementia of Alzheimerâ€™s type patients. Further, the test formulation slowed down the process of cognitive decline in normal elderly people. The test formulation is proposed as a better remedial measure for the prevention and management of cognitive deficits particularly memory problems among elderly people and also in various types of neurodegenerative disorders.

public_title: Morbidity reduction of Lymphatic Filariasis using integrative treatment as self care & home based procedure
scientific_title: Morbidity control of Lymphatic Filariasis using self care Ayurveda & Yoga therapy as pilot in two endemic districts(Alleppey and Gulbarga )
study_type: Ayurveda Yoga & Naturopathy Other (Specify) [ Integrative Medicine]
intervention_name: Skin wash using Soap and warm water, Phanta Soaking, Pre IMLD yoga exercises, Indian manual lymph drainage, Compression bandaging and Post IMLD yoga exercises
intervention_description: Dermatology counseling: Patients attended a counseling session before deciding on treatment. During this process, patients and their family members got complete details of the treatment program. Soap and water wash: Meticulous soap and water wash every day was given by a multipurpose health worker, assisted by the patientâ€™s attendant Phanta soaking: Following the limb wash, the affected limb is immersed in an ayurvedic skin care â€˜â€˜phantaâ€™â€™ solution for 20 minutes. Care of Bacterial entry point: In cases of fungal intertrigo apply clotrimazole 1% cream or amorolfine hydrochloride in sever intractable cases. Ayurvedic herbal dusting powders (avachoornana) are applied on toe web spaces and in the gaps of large folds to absorb moisture. Rasnadi choorna or panchavalkala choorna can be used for absorbing moisture in interdigital web spaces and creases of folds. Rasnadi Choorna is a coarsely powdered mixture of 19 herbs, the main ingredients of which are Pluchea lanceolata root (rasna) and Cedrus deodara stem (devadaru). Many patients have associated gravitational eczema. They were treated with topical betamethasone dipropionate 0.05%. Oozing eczema is initially treated with topical steroids applied under occlusion. Ulcers were treated with cefadroxil 500mg bid x 5 days. Unhealthy granulation tissues and slough on the base of the ulcer are treated with jathyadi thaila, an oil based preparation made of 19 herbs. Yoga exercises: Lymph drainage is achieved by a combination of yoga exercises. Eight yoga exercises (asanas) and five special breathing techniques (pranayamas) are practiced before IMLD, and 10 asanas and five pranayamas are performed afterwards. Yoga DVDs and narrative hand outs are available in IAD but yoga was coached by a therapist during the treatment. Indian manual lymph drainage (IMLD): This is a skin care procedure administered in ayurveda, classified under the broad category of abhyanga . Abhyanga involves massage of the affected parts of the body using both palms while the patient lies supine on a massage table. Part 1 of IMLD (called unmardhana in ayurveda) is a type of non-oil massage that requires the masseur to apply a â€˜â€˜squeezingâ€™â€™pressure using both palms and fingers and moving from the tip of the toes to the upper edge of the lymphoedema. This non-oil massage is performed for 10 minutes with the patient in a supine position. Part 2 of IMLD (udhwarthana ) isa massage using oil. In udhwarthana, oil is smeared to the skin, and the limb is massaged in the opposite direction to hair with more pressure than in general abhyanga. Compression bandaging: After IMLD, disinfected cotton cloth is wrapped around the limb in order to prevent the direct contact with oil of the compression bandages. Long-stretch compression bandages 15 cm in width were used

brief_summary: The project will end by 30th April 2012. Now the study is in the last phase of patient follow up. Write up below is extracts from the report of the evaluation committee approved by the DG of CCRAS, Department of AYUSH Introduction 250 districts in over 15 Indian states are endemic to Lymphatic Filariasis (LF) harboring worlds 1/3 of disease burden. Morbidity control program of GPELF (Global program for elimination of Lymphatic filariasis) being in infancy, no major public health intervention exists except surgery to a small number of patients and advise to wash their limbs. CCRAS (Central Council For Research in Ayurvedic Sciences) under department of AYUSH , Government of India funded a community based intervention trial in two most endemic districts having high poverty index, Alleppey in Kerala and Gulbarga in Karnataka . 1000 patients having unilateral or bilateral lower limb lymphoedema having either grade 2 early , grade 2 late or grade 3 were treated using low cost, self care and home based integrated treatment combining skin wash, ayurvedic skincare, yoga therapy and compression bandaging and bacterial entry point treatment of allopathy. The treatment was implemented by IAD (Institute of Applied Dermatology) at community health centers level at Cherthala in Alleppey and Malkhed in Gulbarga as a public private partnership. This pilot project is in the last phase after completion of patientsâ€™ recruitment and treatment; patients are following up treatment. The project was implemented in two most endemic districts of southern India based on the National Filaria Control Program data: Alleppey of Kerala and Gulbarga of Karnataka. In Gulbarga 3.3% of entire population is affected by this disease. The project is implemented in the model of Innovative Care for Chronic Conditions of WHO. The grading of lymphodema and the conceptual framework of management was as per the guidelines of International Society of Lymphology Consensus Statement 2009. As there are no community level programs for LF in India except an advice to wash their limbs and surgery to minority of patients, this is the pilot program to test if AYUSH treatments integrated with allopathy is effective at the rural communities. The study was conducted as non randomized clinical trial with before and after assessment of outcomes. Because the project used at least three objective parameters as outcome measures, in line with Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions (Version 5) recommendations, non-RCT trial with outcome assessment before and after intervention, is an acceptable design in the current set up, albeit that evaluation committee recognizes RCT as the reference standard methodology. Survey to identify the patients in the community The project adopted a novel method of rapid survey techniques to indentify the patients in the community. First secondary data was collected from district medical office. This data was customized to Cherthala and Malkhed regions. With prior permission for authorities allied health staff such as ASHA workers, village health nurses, health inspectors etc were educated about the LF morbidity reduction program through their monthly meetings. Same strategy was used to motivate the members of CBOs and other local volunteers. Using their contacts, individual patients and clusters of patients were identified and invited for LF camps. Each such camp was used to create awareness with local social leaders, officials and politicians. Treatment delivery and community approach of the project The treatment delivery team was headed by an ayurvedic doctor; assisted by an allopathic staff nurse and master in social work (MSW) to coordinate the community level programs. The patients were selected during LF camps conducted in the villages. Patients of any age, sex, disease grade and duration were recruited. Patients presenting with Acute Dermato Lymphangio Adinitis (cellulitis or filarial fever, also called ADLA) were excluded from the study. All patients received the treatment in the following sequence: soap and water wash, soak with herbalized phanta solution, sequences of yoga exercises with pranayama, Indian manual lymph drainage, compression bandaging and a set of yoga exercise. The treatment was administered as described in international publications titled, â€˜Integrated management of filarial lymphodema for rural communities. Lymphology 2007; 40: 3-13â€™ and â€œIntegrating modern dermatology and Ayurveda in the treatment of vitiligo and lymphedema in India. International Journal of Dermatology, 2011; 50 (3): 310â€“334.â€ Data Collection : Measurement of instrument is appropriate given the studyâ€™s variables. The scoring method is clearly defined. Data on treatment outcomes in LF are maintained in a Microsoft Access database designed and developed by IAD. They are maintained as changes over each limb which is an international consensus. This database can instantly retrieve information using SPSS 16 analysis. Clinical outcome evaluations used were: 1.By recording base line and follow up girth measurements or volume by water displacement method 2.By recording baseline and follow up photos 3.By recording the frequency of â€˜filarial fever episodesâ€™ also known as inflammatory episode 4.By recording the Quality of Life through a validated questionnaire in those patients who have completed the follow ups. Inclusion and exclusion criteria are clearly defined in the patient population selected for the trial. The project treated 1000 patients so far. However there was a selection bias. The treatment team insisted on the participation of at least one member of the family in the treatment program. So those elderly patients who didnâ€™t have any family support were denied the opportunity to take the treatment. Also those patients who were unable to afford the travel cost to the centre couldnâ€™t take the treatment. Dependent t test was used for comparison of limb volumes changes. The study is not complete as two months of follow up is still remaining. Therefore complete statistical analysis was not possible during this evaluation. Based on the available data the project treated 528 lymphoedematous limbs (400 patients) in Alleppey and 659 limbs (600 patients) in Gulbarga. 50 patients dropped out from treatment either for personal reason or were unable to continue the treatment as they found it difficult to follow all procedures. In Alleppey 117 limbs had more than 7 liters of volume (large limb) and 411 limbs were small limbs less than 7 liters. The volume in large limbs reduced from 10.3 liters from baseline to 7.1 liters by 3 months of follow up, small limbs reduced from 5.8 liters from baseline to 4.6 liters at the end of 3 months of follow up. In terms of percentage, large limbs reduced by 39% at the end of 3 months and small limbs by 17.6%. In Gulbarga volume reduction values were 41.4% for large limbs and 22.6% in small limbs at the end of 3 months Other outcome measures used in the trial changed as follows: history of inflammatory episodes was present in 89.3% of limbs (442 limbs) at baseline in Alleppy and at the end of 3months of follow up 5.6% of limbs (9limbs) had the history of inflammatory episode. In Gulbarga the values were 89.7% (540 limbs) and 0.9% (2 limbs) respectively. Bacterial entry points were observed in 80.1% of limbs (401 limbs) and 13% (21 limbs) at the end of 3 months of treatment. In Gulbarga it was observed in 50.3% (302 limbs) at admission and at the end 3months of treatment in 29% (64 limbs). On reversal of lymphoedema grading following treatment , in Alleppy it was observed that 49.8% (73 limbs) were positive for stemmers sign became 5.6%(9 limbs) at the end of 3 months, the values were 12.8%(84 limbs) and to 2.3%(5 limbs) at the end of 3 months for Gulbarga . Quality of life of patients was assessed using a disease specific questionnaire. This was validated, pretested in IAD adopted from WHODAS and VCRC tools but customized for Indian patients. Data of patients who completed three months of followup where analyzed on seven domains. Patients in Alleppey generally presented with the oedema up to groin. In Gulbarga 133 limbs had oedema up to groin or mid thigh and 526 limb had oedema limited to below the knee level. The setting of the study : Although facilities were very much resource poor and restricted, the team provided treatment to an average of 22 patients per day in Cherthala and 28 per day in Malkhed. The team members initially provided this treatment for 9 days and remaining 5 days were used for training these patients for self care along with their family members. This training is itself the treatment for their morbidity reduction. Therefore the study is replicable in any Indian rural settings. Conclusion The treatment is cost effective, easily administrable at remote village level. We estimated a compliance rate of over 40% in the study. However the patients are still following up the treatment and follow up numbers are likely to increase before the project period ends. The reasons for heavy dropout rates are: the distance of patientsâ€™ clusters from the treatment facility although centre was established at the community health centre of the state Government, making access difficult for most patients. Inability to pay for the transport cost, poor connectivity by road are other common reasons. However treatment is effective in the village level as all patients whom evaluators interacted were happy of the outcome and have improved quality of life parameters. This is a model program of self care for LF using AYUSH intervention integrated with allopathy. This is an ayurvedic doctor lead, allopathic nurse assisted model for community dermatology meeting needs of chronic care, acute care and management of infections. The skin care was provided by ayurvedic medicines. Treatment of infections and bacterial entry points were by allopathy and acute episodes of filarial fever that sometimes require hospitalized care was managed by allopathy. Movement essential for prevention of lymph stagnation was achieved by yoga exercises. Compression bandaging of allopathy gave additional lymph drainage to swollen legs.

brief_summary: Present study entitled Concept of Healthy living as mentioned in Ayurvedic classics in relation to Lifestyle disorders (A conceptual and survey study) was carried out with following aims and objectives To explain Healthy living as mentioned in Ayurvedic classics that which may be suitable for present era. A survey study to identify the factors related with life-style in the causation of Sthaulya and Madhumeha . Introduction In the Introduction the research subject Concept of healthy living as mentioned in Ayurvedic classics in relation to lifestyle disorders has been introduced with its need and importance. The present scenario of lifestyle disorders and the potential of Ayurveda in its prevention were specified. The previous work done in similar topics in various institutions of India were also mentioned. Survey Study Madhumaha (Type-2 DM) The present survey study was cross-sectional survey study undertaken to understand the lifestyle related factors of the Madhueha . Total 150 patients of Madhumeha diagnosed with in one year, visiting to the OPD/IPD of IPGT & RA, Jamnagar-Gujarat were surveyed. Observations In the present survey study maximum patients were male (60%), belonging to 41-50 years age group (40%), Married (97.33%), Hindu (88.67%), primary education (31.33%), middle socio-economic status (66.67%) and had sedentary occupation. Maximum patients were having BMI between 25-29.99 (47.34%), maximum patients were having Negative family history (72%) and Chronicity > 8-12 month (41.34%). Maximum patients (58%) reported that they were often taking food when feel good hunger and up to full of stomach (53.33%) and were feeling heaviness after eating. Maximum Patients (56.66%) were reported that they only sometimes pay attention to their hunger level and maximum patients (57.34) used to take food just because it is the time to have food. Majority of the patients (45.34%) reported to take deep fried/ sweet items sometimes in breakfast. Maximum Patients (57.33%) were often taking food containing more oil/ghee/butter. Maximum patients (68%) reported to take more salty food items sometimes and 51.33% patients reported to like more sour taste food items. Maximum patients (47.34%) were taking milk and milk products more than six times in a week, intake of Ghee more than six times in a week was found in 53.67% of patients. Maximum numbers of patients (57.34%) were taking oily and fried food 3-5 times in a week. Intake of potato as vegetables was found very popular and Maximum patients (67.33%) were found to take potato more than 3-5 times in a week. In present survey study it was found that 60.67% patients were never doing exercise or going for brisk walk in the morning/evening, 89.34% patients were never doing Yoga Asana etc. It was found that 28.66% patients often and 26.67% patients almost always sleep in day time. 67.33% of patients sometimes suppress natural urge of defecation, urination etc. In present survey study it was found that 57.34% patients are not at all happy considering all the things in life, 59.34% patients no more than usual enjoying their day to day activities. Maximum patients (65.33%) were found to feel lazy for doing work more than usual. Sthaulya (Obesity) Cross-sectional survey study on Sthaulya was undertaken to understand the lifestyle related factors involved in the causation of disease. Total 250 Sthaulya patients were surveyed visiting to the OPD/IPD of IPGT & RA, Jamnagar-Gujarat. Observations In the present survey study of Sthaulya (Obesity) maximum patients were female (83.2%), belonging to 31-40 years age group (34.8%), Married (87.2%), Hindu (80.8%), secondary level education (34.4%), middle socio-economic status (79.6%) and had sedentary type of occupation. Maximum patients (45.6%) were having BMI between 30-34.9; maximum patients were having Negative family history (48.8%) and Chronicity > 5 years (54.8%). In present Survey study it was found that maximum 60% patients were often taking food when feel good hunger and 44.4% patients were sometimes taking food just because it is the time to have food, 50.4% patients were often eating up to full of stomach and feel heaviness after eating. Most of the patients (44.8%) were sometimes taking deep fried food/sweets/non-veg in their breakfast. It was found that 56.8% of patients were often taking food containing more oil, ghee or butter and 51.2% of patients were almost always drinking water immediately after having food. 27.2% patients more than 6 times and 27.2% 3-5 times were taking milk and milk products, 53.6% of patients were taking ghee more than 6 times in a week. It was found that maximum 52.8% of patients were taking oily and fried food 3-5 times in a week. Use of potatoes as vegetables was found very popular and 63.6% patients were taking Potatoes 3-5 times in a week. In present survey it was found that 61.6% patients were never doing any exercise or going for brisk walk in morning/evening time, 84% patients were never doing Yoga, Asana etc. and 92% patients were reported to never participating actively in sportive or physical activities. It was reported that 35.6% of patients were almost always and 24.8% of patients were often, sleeping in day time, 33.2% patients almost always and 25.6% were often sleeping immediately after having food in day time. Maximum patients (42.8%) were enjoying sleeping for long time in morning and maximum patients (56.8%) were reported to rarely wake up before 6 am. In present survey study it was found that 46% of patients were feeling happy no more than usual and 32% patients were not at all happy considering all the things in life. 66.8% patients were feeling lazy for doing work more than usual. Discussion Madhumeha Data of 150 surveyed Madhumeha (type-2 DM) patients was analysed by calculating percentage to determine the lifestyle related factors responsible for the manifestation of disease. Obtained results from survey were discussed in detail. In present survey study maximum patients (72%) were having negative family history it strongly suggest that sedentary lifestyle, faulty food habits and psychological distress were the chief etiological factors behind manifestation of Madhumeha . Sthaulya Total 250 Sthaulya patients were surveyed and the data was analysed by calculating percentage to determine the main lifestyle related factors involved in the causation of the diseases. In Gujarat state, especially in Jamnagar area it was found that people are less physically active and take food rich in fat and sugar, and if more calories are consumed than expended, the excess calories are stored as fat. Such lifestyle pattern is definitely a cause of weight gain and Sthaulya . All the lifestyle related factors were discussed in detail with supportive classical and modern references. Conclusion From present survey study of Madhumeha and Sthaulya it can be concluded that intake of heavy, fatty food, physical inactivity, habit of day sleep and psychological imbalance are the main factors associated in the manifestation of disease.

brief_summary: Inflammation is a cascade of reactions by the body in response to harmful stimuli which can be in the form of pathogens or cuts and bruises. It is natural protective mechanism and helps to start the healing process. However, inflammatory disorders occur when there is abnormal inflammation and are associated with immune system. Inflammation can be both acute and chronic in nature. Acute inflammation usually occurs immediately within minutes and can last up to a few days. However chronic inflammation has a delayed onset and lasts longer. KAL-13/KAL-13 Plus are Ayurvedic formulations designed to treat inflammatory disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, pain management, inflammatory bowel disease, colitis, COPD (pulmonary inflammation), multiple sclerosis and psoriasis. KAL-13 is an herbal preparation based on Ayurveda. KAL-13 Plus is composition including microgram quantities of mineral and amino acids added to KAL 13. These formulations contain Ayurvedic herbs prepared by a proprietary method for enhanced efficacy. Based on the positive data from the pre-clinical studies for KAL-13 and KAL-13 Plus, a clinical trial in human was conducted in osteoarthritic patients as per GCP guidelines at Banaras Hindu University, India. The primary objectives are to study - Reduction in signs and symptoms of osteoarthritis, Change from baseline in the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities (WOMAC) 3.1 osteoarthritis Index Composite, Pain, Morning Stiffness and Physical Function subscale scores. The secondary objective is assessment of osteoarthritis by Kellgren and Lawrence scoring/grading.

brief_summary: The present study is randomized parallel, double arm clinical study to compare effect of Gomutra Haritaki with and without Langhana and Pachana. Gomutra Haritaki described in Ashtanga Hridaya Samhita Chikitsa Sthana 8/55, consists of Haritaki (Terminalia chebula retz.) and Gomutra (cow urine). For the preparation of Gomutra Haritaki, Haritaki(1 part) was boiled until Gomutra (2.5 part) evaporated and the granules of semisolid consistency were punched into tablets of 500 mg each. Total 153 patients were registered for the present clinical trial. In Group A, 76 patients were registered, out of them 70 patients completed the treatment while in Group B, 77 patients were registered and out of them 68 patients completed the treatment. Group A, Langhana and Pachana followed by Gomutra Haritaki For the purpose of Langhana (light diet) i.e., one time regular meal (lunch) and Mudga Yusha(green gram soup) in dinner for 4 days was advised. This was followed by Pachana for 10 days with Dhanyaka-Shunthi Sidhha Jala. Dhanyaka-Shunthi Sidhha Jala was prepared by mixing of 400 ml of water with 6 gm drug [ 4.5 gm Dhanyaka (coriandrum sativum Linn.) and 1.5 gm Shunthi (zingiber officinale Rosc.) ] was boiled until 200 ml water was evaporated. This medicated water was given for twice a day at morning and evening 6 pm. After 10 days of Pachana, Gomutra Haritaki was administered in the dose of 500 mg each, 2 tablets with luke warm water (Ushnodaka) before food thrice a day for 8 weeks. Group B, Placebo capsules followed by Gomutra Haritaki For initial 14 days, 2 capsules (starch powder) of 500 mg each twice daily were given to compare the effect of placebo with Langhana and Pachana. During this period no diet restriction was done. Followed by placebo capsules, Gomutra Haritaki was administered 2 tablets 500 mg each with luke warm water before food thrice a day for 8 weeks. Patients were assessed before treatment, after 14 days Langhana-Pachana or placebo treatment and after treatment, bio chemical parameters-lipid profile were also done during this interval. Results: After 14 days of course with Langhana and Pachana in Group A, S. Cholesterol (7.66%), S. Triglyceride (13.56%), S.LDL (7.89%), S.VLDL (15.39%) were decreased which were statistically significant. S.HDL was decreased by 3.36% which was statistically insignificant. In Group B where only placebo treatment was given without diet restriction. S.Cholesterol (0.51%), S. Triglyceride (2.20%), S.VLDL (3.24%), S.HDL (1.15%) were increased which were statistically insignificant. S.LDL was decreased by 0.01% which was statistically insignificant. Over all effect of therapy which was calculated by difference at baseline and after administration of Gomutra Haritaki showed that in Group A, S. Cholesterol (8.59%), S.Triglyceride (8.72%), S.LDL(11.45%), S.VLDL (10.76%) were decreased which were statistically significant. S.HDL was decreased by 2.11% which was statistically insignificant where in Group B, S.Cholesterol (9.51%), S. Triglyceride (7.91%), S.LDL (13.14%), S.VLDL (7.63%) were decreased which were also statistically significant. S.HDL was decreased by 2.5% which was statistically insignificant. After applying unpaired t test for comparison of overall effect of Group A and B, it was found that difference of results reported in their Groups on S.Cholesterol, S.Triglyceride, S.LDL, S.VLDL, S.HDL were statistically insignificant. In Group A, lipid profile was decreased significantly after Langhana and Pachana of 14 days and almost remained stable after administration of Gomutra Haritaki while in Group B no change was observed after placebo for 14 days but lipid profile was significantly reduced after administration of Gomutra Haritaki.

brief_summary: Central obesity is a leading preventable cause of death worldwide, with increasing prevalance in adults and children , and authorities view it as one of the most serious public health problems of the 21st century. It is defined as to the presence of excess fat in the abdominal area. Of late, it has been shown that it has positive correlation with insulin resistance and is a strong risk factor for cardiovascular diseases and a strong predictor of future diabetes mellitus. This realization has brought t he concept of measuring waist circumference as an indicator of insulin resistance. T he clustering of central obesity ( waist circumference â‰¥ 90 cm for men and â‰¥ 80cm for women, with ethnicity specific values for Asian-Indian population ) along with any two among raised triglycerides level (â‰¥ 150 mg/dL), reduced high density lipoprotein cholesterol (< 40 mg/dL in males and < 50 mg/dL in females) , raised blood pressure (systolic BP â‰¥ 130 or diastolic BP â‰¥ 85 mm Hg), raised fasting plasma glucose (â‰¥ 100 mg/dL) is defined as metabolic syndrome (syndrome x) . It is estimated that 20%â€“25% of south Asians have developed metabolic syndrome and many more may be prone to it. There is currently no treatment to manage the metabolic syndrome. Many studies are looking at treatment that might improve some of the symptoms of metabolic syndrome. The clinical features of metabolic syndrome is nearer to Lakshanas of Medoroga, hence metabolic syndrome may be compared to Medoroga. Medoroga is a Santarpanajanya vikara where in Srotorodha, improper Agni and disarrangement of Tridosha are present. Virechana karma is one the treatment modality for treating Santarpanajanya vikaras . Virechana karma clears the Srotoavarodha, normalizes the Agni and brings homeostasis of Tridoshas.Hence it may be hypothesize that Virechana karma may be beneficial for treating Medoroga (metabolic syndrome).

brief_summary: SUMMARY Total 31 patients were registered and randomly divided into two groups, Group A and Group B. Out of the 15 patients registered in Group A, 14 completed the study and 1 left against medical advice. In Group B, total 16 Patients were registered, out of which 15 completed the trial, and 1 patient could not continue the treatment. Though both the groups were statistically insignificant on objective parameters, but Group A ( Virechana followed by Shamana ) showed better results on subjective parameters than Group B ( Shamana ). Looking at the chronic nature and gradual onset of the disease, sufficient duration is required to cure Ama and Agnimandya at Dhatu level. Results could have been more effective if the trial would have been continued for longer duration. Hence, Null hypothesis is rejected and alternative hypothesis is accepted. Virechana followed by Shamana therapy ( Triphladya Guggulu and Punarnavadi Kashaya ) is more effective in the management of Hypothyroidism than Shamana therapy alone ( Triphladya Guggulu and Punarnavadi Kashaya ).

brief_summary: This study is a randomized, double blind, parallel group, multi-centre placebo controlled clinical study of Ayurvedic coded drug â€˜Ayush Aâ€™ in the management of mild bronchial asthma (Tamaka Shwasa) that will be conducted in three center in India. The primary outcome measures will be change in asthma controlled questionnaire (ACQ) from the baseline and at the end of 12 th week, PEFR assessments of personal best peak flow every 14 th days to the end of the trial. The secondary outcome measures will be the change in St. Georgeâ€™s respiratory questionnaire (SGRQ-C) from the baseline and at the end of 12 th week. Bronchial Asthma is an inflammatory disorder of the airways characterized by increased responsiveness of the trachea and bronchi to various stimuli resulting in narrowing of the airways due to bronchial spasm and edema in bronchial mucous membrane. These changes are reversible either spontaneously or with medication. It may be acute or paroxysmal in type. Most asthmatic patients are diagnosed by triad episodic symptoms (wheezing, cough and dyspnea). In older people, it is not easy to differentiate whether it is certainly a case of asthma, as these symptoms are also seen in other diseases because of poor respiratory function due to ageing. Bronchial Asthma is increasing day by day with the increase in pollution levels and the stressful lifestyle. The prevalence of asthma in elderly people varies from 6.5 to 10%, however the incidence is dependent on environmental condition, occupational patterns, genetic configuration and dietary pattern of the population besides diagnostic criteria adopted by different investigators. Bronchial Asthma is similar to disease entity â€œ Tamaka Svasa â€ described in ayurveda . Tamaka svasa is a condition in which difficulty in breathing occurred due to the obstruction to pranavayu due to vitiated kapha . According to ayurveda , main causes of tamaka svasa are unwholesome diet ( vidahi, guru, ruksa, abhisyandi diet), exposure to allergen (cold air, dust, smoke, etc.), excessive exertion, etc., which are very close to etiology of bronchial asthma.

brief_summary: The symptoms of insomnia and excessive somnolence in association with some degree of social, occupational, or other impairment are collectively known as Shift Work Sleep Disorder (SWSD) [i] . ICD 10 identifies the condition under Circadian rhythm Sleep Disorders G47.26 [ii] whereas DSM IV classification identifies under 307.45 [iii] . The symptoms may range from gastrointestinal disorders, metabolic disorders, immunity disorders, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and reproductive issues to neurological issues [iv] .Shift work related sleep disorders causes significant changes in individualsâ€™ physical, occupational, cognitive, and social functioning, which also decreases their quality of life (QoL) [v] , [vi] . Night shift workers with symptomatic SWSD fulfilling the eligibility criteria will be incidentally selected who are voluntarily willing to participate in the study. Their baseline data will be obtained using Socio-demographic characteristics, PQSI, WHO QoL, Agnibala, dehabala and Satwabala . The selected workers will be advised to follow following lifestyle modification; to sleep half of the time of usual sleep before food intake. The workers are advised to maintain a sleep log to confirm sleeping/sleep loss pattern for a fortnight. The final evaluation will be done after study duration of 2 weeks. brief_summary: Infertility is defined as failure to conceive more than one year of regular & unprotected coitus. It is emotionally involved with a lot of social stigma. Infertility divided into 2 types: Primary - patients who have never conceived . Secondary - Indicates previous proven pregnancy but fails to conceive subsequently. Correlating fallopian tubes with the Artavavaha (Artava-beeja-vaha) Srotas , its block can be compared as Sanga type of Srotodushti . Abnormality of tubes is generally of two types:- (1)Structural - Anatomical blockage - due to vitiation of Vata-Kapha / Pitta Kapha (2) Functional - defect in cilliary function of tube -due to vitiation of Vata . Tubal block -30% The management of infertility due to tubal factor in modern depends upon the site of blockage: includes Tubal Microsurgery, Tubal Adhesiolysis, Fimbrioplasty, I.V.F., Tube re-canalization. But all these methods have its own limits; success rate 50-60%in isthmic block. Moreover all these methods are the solution only for the anatomical aspect of the tube and no success in establishing the tubal function. So it is the time to develop a safe, established, cost effective and permanent cure Ayurvedic protocol for this sensitive problem. Virechana ( Samshodhana therapy) is a biocleansing method meant for cleaning of micro channels (minute Strotas ). Fallopian tube can be correlated with micro channel related to Aartavvaha strotas . So any obstruction in fallopian tube can be removed by Virechana Karma . Uttarabasti [Intra Uterine Uttarabasti (IUUB)] with various medicated oil / ghee is an unique procedure mentioned in Ayurvedic classics especially for the treatment of Vandhyatva, Artavadusti and other Yoniroga (All gynecological disorders), where other treatments become failure. So keeping hypothesis in mind for opening of the tube, Apamarga Kshara Taila will be used because of its Lekhana (scraping) property , Phalkalyana Ghrita for Ropana and better function of (cillary movement) fallopian tube and to promote conception.

brief_summary: Total 44 Thalassemic patients were registered for this study as 22 in each group A and B. out of them 1 patient in group A was discontinued due to various reasons and rest 43 patients completed the course. Group A patients were given the trial drugs i.e. Modified Musta-Triphaladi Avaleha and Gandhakadi Yoga Tablets along with the modern medical management. With anupana Ushnodaka and doses as per youngâ€™s formula. While group B was the control group where patients were undergone only modern medical management (blood transfusion and iron chelation). Treatment period and follow-up were 12 weeks each and subjective and objective parameters of all patients were assessed before and after the treatment. After 12 weeks of treatment, overall effect of therapy showed that, in Group A, 10 (47.61%) patients got maximum improvement, 6(28.57%) patients got moderate improvement and 5 (23.80%) patients got mild improvement. No improvement was not seen in any patient. In Group B none of the patients got maximum improvement, moderate improvement, mild improvement and in all 22 patients (100%) got no improvement. On comparing subjective, objective parameters, BT Interval and general health status, trial group was found to be far better than control group. Modified Musta-Triphaladi Avaleha and Gandhakadi Yoga have effective role as an adjuvant along with the conventional approach in the management of Thalassemia Major.

brief_summary: PURPOSE OF THE STUDY: Regarding the time of administration of Niruha Basti, it is said to be given to a person who is not too hungry after the Jeernanna Lakshanas are observed which is usually seen in Pratah Kala. Also, the person should have voided urine and faeces. There is another opinion that it should be administered in Madhyahna Kala, specifically Madhyahne Kinjith Avarthe which means some time after the commencement of Madhyahna. So a need has been felt, to find out whether Niruha Basti Pranidhana Kala is significant while evaluating the effect of Basti in a disease and does it have any influence on the assessment of Samyak Niruda Lakshanas. So the present study is planned to evaluate the effect of different Pranidhana Kala of Niruha Basti. AIM: To assess the variation of response to Erandamooladi Niruha Basti in Gridrasi depending on time of administration OBJECTIVES OF THE STUDY: 1)To assess the variation of response to Erandamooladi Niruha Basti administered as Yoga basti in Gridrasi in Madhyahna Kala 2) To assess the variation of response to Erandamooladi Niruha Basti administered as Yoga basti in Gridrasi in Pratah Kala 3) To compare the response to Erandamooladi Niruha Basti administered as Yoga basti in Gridrasi in Madhyahna Kala and Pratah Kala MATERIALS AND METHODS: Open label double armed, randomised, clinical trial with appropriate sample size conducted in Amrita School of Ayurveda. Pre-diagnosed patients of Gridrasi fulfilling inclusion criteria will be taken for study and randomly divided into 2 groups namely Group Madhyahna Kala (GMK) and Group Pratah Kala (GPK). In both groups, the patients will receive Sthanika Abhyanga on Udara and Prishta regions for 5 minutes with Sahacharadi Thaila followed by Nadisweda with Ushnajala before administration of Niruha Basti. The time of administration of Basti will be recorded daily. After Pratyagamana of Basti Dravya, the patient is advised to take Ushnajala Snana followed by intake of rice gruel. Anuvasana Basti will be administered soon after the lunch. Group GMK: The patients will be given light breakfast (3 Idli / Dosa with tea or the equal quantity of other materials) in the morning at 8.00 am. Niruha Basti will be administered in Madhyahna Kala (between 11.30 am to 12.30 pm) after Jeernahara Lakshanas are observed when the patient is not too hungry as per the schedule. Group GPK: Niruha Basti will be administered in the morning hours (between 7.30am to 8.30 am) on the empty stomach when the patient is not too hungry and Jeernahara Lakshanas are observed. In both groups, the patients will receive Yoga basti with Sahacharadi Thaila Anuvasana Basti and Erandamooladi Niruha Basti. The patients will receive Yoga basti with Sahacharadi Thaila Anuvasana Basti and Erandamooladi Niruha Basti. ASSESSMENT CRITERIA: The assessment will be done at the baseline and after treatment based on the clinical changes observed in the patients. Self-gradation will be done for the assessment parameters. Subjective Parameters: Samyak Basti Lakshanas, Improvement in the signs and symptoms of Gridrasi, Visual analogue scale for pain (numeric rating scale), SLR test and Roland-Morris Disability Scale. Objective Parameters: Range of movement of the lumbar spine with the goniometer, walking time, walking distance and standing time.

The impact of dementia on caregivers, family and societies can be physical, psychological, social and economical. With the modern therapeutics, though there is spectacular achievement in providing relief in the patients of dementia, still a high risk exists due to serious side effects of therapy. Recently there is tremendous urge to explore medicinal plants globally for improving cognitive function owing to their less adverse effects. These drugs are having Aayuprada, Aamayanashana, Bala, Agni, Varna, Swara vardhaka and Medhya properties , Hence this study is conceptualized using Medhya Rasayan a. The present study involves oral administration of Medhya Rasayanas as churna containing Mandukparni, Guduchi, Shankhapushpi and Yashtimadhu . These herbs are been extensively researched for their Nootropic effects . This is a humble effort to evaluate the efficacy of Medhya Rasayana of dementia of the Alzheimerâ€™s type .

brief_summary: Hypothesis- Silk hair of corn (Makkaya) kshara is effective in the management of cholelitheasis Cholelithiasis (gall bladder stone) is a crystalline concretion formed within the gall bladder by accretion of bile components. A study shows that more than 85% of people having gall stones will be asymptomatic even for years. Presence of stones in gall bladder, either symptomatic or asymptomatic may lead to acute or chronic cholecystitis and presence of stones in other parts of biliary tract can cause obstruction of bile ducts, which can lead to serious conditions as ascending cholangitis or pancreatitis. Any of these conditions can be life threatening and are considered to be surgical emergencies and require compulsory cholecystectomy. The drugs to dissolve gall stones or other non surgical methods are still considered experimental in modern medicine. By over all view it is very much clear that treatment prescribed in modern medicine for Cholelithiasis is far from satisfactory and is often accompanied with several side effects. So there is large scope in Ayurveda in the field of management of Cholelithiasis. Acharya Sushruta very specifically indicates Paneeya Kshara in the management of Ashmari and the Kshara due to its ksharana property can easily dissolve Ashmari. silk hair of Makkaya is having Diuresis and Kaliuresis effect. Hence in Cholelithiasis, considering it as Pittashayagata Ashmari, use of Paneeya Kshara prepared out of Silk hair of corn (Makkaya)being made here is expected to contribute towards better management of Cholelithiasis

brief_summary: Non alcoholic Fatty Liver Syndrome (NAFLD) is now regarded as the hepatic manifestation of metabolic syndrome. Three lifestyle diseases i.e. Diabetes, obesity and hyperlipidemia are considered as risk factors. 70% Non-alcoholic Steatohepatitis had one or more of the above risk factors. Prevalence of NAFLD in asymptomatic middle-aged patients is as high as 46.0%. When they continue the same life style it will lead to fatty liver infiltration and then to liver cirrhosis or even liver cancer. So an early intervention that reverses the pathology might decrease the morbidity and mortality rate. Current treatment focuses on decreasing insulin resistance, Cholesterol management and Weight loss . Studies on drugs like metformin, thiazolidinediones prescribed for NAFLD are found to have significant side effects. Bariatric surgery has been proved as effective but is expensive. Studies on first-line treatment approach to NAFLD based on diet and lifestyle modification are nonrandomized and short term. Due to paucity of data it is difficult to produce evidence-based recommendations about dietary modifications and exercise in NAFLD patients. Moreover, dietary treatment alone is limited by the lack of compliance and the frequent regain of weight at follow-up. So an Ayurveda treatment protocol that is safe and inexpensive, effective in the reversal of first grade fatty liver is the need of the hour. Subjects who meet inclusion criteria and are willing to participate in the study will be assigned into two groups of 50 each according to Simple Random Sampling method. They are 1) Control Group:- for whom Ayurveda Diet and Exercise shall be prescribed and 2) Trial Group:- for whom Ayurveda Diet , Exercise and Ayurveda medicine shall be prescribed . At baseline all study subjects will be screened for blood lipid profile, LFT, and US abdomen to confirm diagnosis. For the Control Group Diet preparations wholesome diet suitable for diabetes ,obesityand dyslipedemia shall be given. Exercise regimen shall be according to their BMI, Occupation, Constitution , Season and Strength. For the Trial Group apart from Ayurveda Diet and exercise, treatment aiming at treatment for reducing fat, increasing digestive power, that increases digestion and due regulation of dosha followed by hepato protective Rasayana will be prescribed. Each group shall be constantly monitored separately for three months. Blood tests done at base line will be repeated in participants who successfully complete the treatment within the prescribed time. Pre test post comparison of the quantitative variables will be analysed by paired t test or Wilcoxon signed rank test according to the nature of the data. Pre test post test comparison of qualitative variables will be analysed by McNemar test. Between groups differences of the quantitative variables will be evaluated by independent sample test. A p-value of < 0.05 will be considered as the level of significant. Data analysis will be performed using SPSS ver 17.0.

brief_summary: Prameha is a Tridoshajavyadhi but the predominance of Dosha and Dooshya enables its classification into Vataja, Pitaja & Kaphaja Pramehas. Major symptoms of Prameha (Prediabetes) are Prabhuta Mutrata (Polyuria), Avila Mutrata (Turbidity in urine), Mutra Madhurya, Pipasa - Adhika (Polydipsia), Kshudha- Adhika ((polyphagia), Swedadhikya (Perspiration), Karapadadaha( burning sensation in palm and sole), Alasya/Utsahahani (lethargy/ lack of enthusiasm) and Nidradhikya ( excessive Sleep). Prediabetes is one of the major clinically entity, striking resemblance with that of Prameha and Diabetes Mellitus having close resemblance with Madhumeha. Lifestyle and dietary errors are the major etiological categories described for Prameha, which closely resemble with the etiology of Prediabetes. In Prameha Chikitsa Acharyas have specifically emphasized on use of Shodhana Chikitsa. Vamana Karma (therapeutic emesis) and Virechana Karma (therapeutic purgation) are indicated in Sthula Pramehi. Variuos Aushad Yogas are also mentioned in the classics for the management of Prameha. Nidana Parivarjana and Pathya Aahar Vihar have a significant role in the prevention and management of Prameha/ Prediabetes. The study will conducted on 90 clinically diagnosed & confirmed cases of Prameha / Prediabetes from OPD & IPD section of National institute of Ayurveda Jaipur and community screening. The patients will be equally and randomly divided into three groups with 30 patients each Viz Group. A (Vamana Karma with Madanphala Yoga and Virechana with Abhayaadi modaka), Group.B (Darvayadi Ghanavati Yoga) and Group C: Lifestyle modification. Written consent will be taken from the patient before starting trial. Assessment will be done before treatment, after treatment and during last follow up. Observations and results of the treatments will be compared and statistically tested. Conclusion will be drawn on the basis of observations and finding of statistical analysis.

brief_summary: National AYUSH Mission (NAM) of Ministry of AYUSH, Govt. of India states Operational Guidelines for AYUSH Services wherein it has clearly mentioned the Core/essential activities viz. Co-location of AYUSH facilities at PHCs, CHCs and District Hospitals, Upgradation of Government AYUSH Hospitals, AYUSH Dispensaries, Public outreach activity and Behavioural Change Communication (BCC)/ Information Education and Communication etc. 1 Behaviour change communication (BCC) is widely recognized as one of the main health promotion strategies. It is an interactive process of working with individuals and communities to develop communication strategies to promote positive behaviours as well as create a supportive environment to enable them to adopt and sustain positive behaviours. The primary objectives of BCC in public health programmes, are to modify lifestyles which risk individual well-being, and to achieve health-improvements and environmental change. 2 India is shifting from communicable diseases to non- communicable diseases (NCDs). Early prevention and case detection is the most important strategy of all non-communicable diseases including cancer which are generally emerged due to lifestyle deviations and ill-healthy diet. Disease prevention, promotion of health and specific intervention considering patient and environmental and dietary factor are the strengths of AYUSH systems. NAM support for BCC strategy incorporating AYUSH strengths in early prevention of such NCDs which will be advocated by the health providers (AYUSH physicians). 1 Cancer is a major component of morbidity and mortality in India and world over. Cancer, Precancerous states have multidimensional presentations and modes of development and spread. The current research findings have brought to light that Cancer is both preventable and treatable provided the physicians and common people have clear understanding about how cancer is caused, how to identify it in the earliest possible form and how to choose correct treatment modalities. Ayurvedic Faculty is a strong health care force spread across the length and breadth of India and as said earlier Government of India has recognized the sheer potential of this group and has taken initiatives to collocate them along with Allopathy dispensaries, hospital across country under schemes like NRHM. It is also a well-known fact that most of the rural India the Ayurvedic physicians play a vital role in delivering health care services. Ayurvedic graduates are trained in both traditional and modern methods of diagnosis and are expected to identify any precancerous or cancerous condition in its very early forms. BCC is the comprehensive process which involves various steps and involves various stakeholders including healthcare providers in the community in it. A Knowledge Attitude Practice (KAP) survey is a representative study of a specific population to collect information on what is known, believed and done in relation to a particular topic. In most KAP surveys, data are collected using a structured, standardized questionnaire. KAP survey data are essential to help plan, implement and evaluate Advocacy, Communication and social mobilisation (ACSM) work. A survey could also be designed to explore ways to involve all health providers including outpatient government services, hospitals, and NGOs. The data collected enable programme managers to set programme priorities, to estimate resources required for various activities, to select the most effective communication channels and messages, to establish baseline levels and measure change that results from interventions, and for advocacy (e.g. to show the magnitude of a challenge, which in turn, may inform resource needs). 3 Various KAP studies have been carried out in India and abroad on various themes and cancer also. However as per published literature, any KAP study is not conducted in Cancer and Ayurvedic fraternity hence it becomes essential to conduct this study. The survey data will serve as baseline data which will help in designing the BCC strategy for Cancer and its better implementation in the community.

brief_summary: Unacceptable taste of oral medication has been the challenge to the medical fraternity since time immemorial, more so with Ayurvedic system of medicine. Oral administration of bitter medicated ghee/oil in increased dosage pattern (Snehapana) as a part of detox treatment in Ayurveda system of medicine has been major hurdle in clinical practice. However, this procedure yielding promising results, Ayurvedic practitioners seldom or never compromise with the concept of Snehapana procedure. This particular factor, many a time leads to the rejection of medication or less acceptance of Ayurveda system of medicine among public or patients. Nano-encapsulation of this dosage form of medicated ghee would resolve the incompatibility and bring palatability and acceptability. To rule out the possibilities of loss of bioactive agents in the process of nano-ecapsulation, a comparative clinical evaluation of the same will be done with conventional medication in the management of selective dermatological disorders.
